newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CS Holding stock, options up in pre-bourse.
newsitem.headline: CS Holding stock, options up in pre-bourse.

text.p: Pre-bourse trading in share options in CS Holding was lively following news late Monday that the Swiss financial group had sold its stake in the industrial activities of Elektrowatt.
Shares in Elektrowatt were also firmer, but dealers added the deal had effectively put a cap on the price.

CS Holding's registered shares were quoted 50 cents firmer at 137.75/138.25 francs as dealers welcomed the news that CS Holding finally had completed the sale of most of its 44.9 percent stake in Elektrowatt.

CS Holding will sell its stake in Elektrowatt's industrial activities to Siemens AG of Germany for 285 francs per share. On Friday CS Holding announced it was selling its stake in Elektrowatt's power activities -- grouped in Watt AG -- for 265 francs per share to a Swiss-German consortium.
This amounts to a total price of 550 francs that CS Holding will get for its Elekrowatt shares, or just over two billion francs.
Both Siemens and the Swiss-German consortium will make public offers for the rest of the Elektrowatt shares.
"The move is undoubtedly positive for CS Holding, but now there is no imagination left in Elektrowatt's shares," said a dealer, noting there is no reason to pay more than 550 francs for the shares.
Elektrowatt's shares rose around five percent to 535/538 francs in pre-bourse trading.
The completion of CS Holding's divestment of Elektrowatt also clears the deck for Lukas Muehlemann, who will take over as chief executive of the Credit Suisse Group next year.
Muehlemann, who helped rejuvenate Swiss Reinsurance, is expected to help Credit Suisse in its restructuring process.
The "M" factor, where "M" stands for Muehlemann, was a key ingredient in the rise in Swiss Re's shares in the last two years and some banks have already tipped CS Holding as the share of 1997.
